correctness.rationale: Fourier inversion on the M modulation frequencies makes orthonormality equivalent to each 3x3 fiber matrix H_j having mutually orthogonal rows. Along the k-translation cycle, any consecutive three projective vectors are orthogonal, forcing projective period 3; therefore order t=N/gcd(N,k) must be divisible by three. When 3|t, d residue cycles in Z_M of length M/d each admit exactly six projective line patterns, determined by a cyclic permutation matrix and the unique order-three complex Hadamard/cyclic triple conditions; each of M free phase scalars yields q^M choices iff 3|q. Therefore count=6^d q^M, normalized count=6^d q^(M-1), and continuous solutions form exactly 6^d copies of T^M. Independent direct fiber tests covered 33 parameter cases / 94809 arrays, plus direct complex full Gram checks in inspected verifier; these do not replace cycle proof.
